items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: I always think of this analogous thing that Somerset Maugham wrote about a man who lived as a beach-comber on a beautiful island and when someone asked the writer how the man died, or why he died, he said, 'I think it was the beauty of it all that killed him.'

ctx.x: And Bix was an educated man and he had great regard for the theatre, books, for anything artistic. It wasn't just music, but in the short time that Tesh and Bix were to live, they lived full lives, if being dedicated to music can be considered a full life, and I certainly would agree that it can be.

I always think of this analogous thing that Somerset Maugham wrote about a man who lived as a beach-comber on a beautiful island and when someone asked the writer how the man died, or why he died, he said, 'I think it was the beauty of it all that killed him.'
